gaps.note: MegaETH had no network unit in cycle 20, and only theme-outside-signature-senders touched it, on the deposit path. No battery, targeted set or script set was rerun at the current replica build, and the block producer is still closed (L-875, high, open since cycle 18). The critic query of 2026-11-25 to https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc answered mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42@mnet-ash-rpc-2, the build no cycle has tied to a source revision. The only evidence for the producer is mined blocks re-executed in the public stateless validator, which cycle 19 stopped at block 32,826,734 plus 2,061 blocks of the network unit.

Monad had no network unit in cycle 20. The endpoint answered Monad/0.16.7 to the critic query of 2026-11-25, and the release page still puts validators on v0.16.5. No vector rerun this cycle, and no release note since v0.16.7 was read.

Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche had no network unit in cycle 20, and Polygon Salvador and BNB Chain Jenner activate on 8 December 2026. Only theme units touched them (evidence audit, multicoin, reserved routing), and none reran the battery or the script sets. Critic query of 2026-11-25: bor/ebcfea01452d/v2.11.1-private on the publicnode endpoint, which refuses past-block reads without a token, and Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247 on bsc-dataseed1, which has no state for old blocks.

Ethereum and the seven OP Stack chains with ETH gas had no network unit in cycle 20. Ethereum has not had one since before cycle 16, although its reth nodes run evm2 with ruint 1.21.1, the same arithmetic code as Tempo. The ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com endpoint in networks.json returned HTTP 403 to a batched request from the critic on 2026-11-25, so any tool that batches against it needs another endpoint.

Every Arc clearance on the value frame hook and the SELFDESTRUCT replacement was read from the main branch or from tags. stablecoin-l1 found that the commits the endpoints report (37812c61 on rpc.mainnet.arc.io, 8e8edb7a on arc.drpc.org) return 404 on raw.githubusercontent.com, so the code that runs on Arc is not in the public history. The endpoint answered arc/v1 to the critic query, which names no build. Native payouts (P1) pass through that hook on every take of address(0).

The Go toolchain readings stop at go1.26.11. theme-evidence-audit read the release branch logs for go1.25.6 to go1.25.13 and go1.26.0 to go1.26.11, but Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain run nitro rc.9 built with go1.27.3, and the go1.27 fix list was not read in any cycle. Arbitrum One answered linux-arm64 and Robinhood Chain answered linux-amd64 and linux-arm64 inside one three element batch to the critic query of 2026-11-25, so batching does not pin an architecture on Robinhood Chain, and no rerun there is known to have been answered by one architecture only.

The HyperEVM validator is closed, and the only public archive endpoint still runs nanoreth nb-20261110. The new release nb-20261125-2 moves to revm 43.0.3 and ruint 1.20.1 and turns on memory_limit, and the team asked operators to run it for compatibility with hl-node, which suggests hl-node moves too. No cycle read the code that ruint 1.20.1 adds: its changelog entry #634 reimplements shifts by primitive integer types without truncating large amounts (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/main/CHANGELOG.md, fetched by the critic). The official endpoint answers past blocks with head state, and the critic confirmed it: eth_getCode of the PoolManager at block 1 returned 24,009 bytes.

theme-mined-gas-cap measured claim redemption under the mined cap on 14 networks only. These seven had no holder list because their log endpoints were rate limited. The exit measurement covers all 21.
Contradiction: hyperevm rates F-020 medium and its verifier rates it high (operator), citing SCHEMA.md for a freeze or loss that needs a validator vote. The ledger needs one value.
Contradiction: op-stack-custom-gas files the X Layer trie seek finding as info and its verifier as low, for an operational hazard with no loss path. The verifier's reading matches SCHEMA.md.

Contradiction resolved by the verifier: arbitrum-family says the Elysium pmdiff2 script that differs was not identified again, and its verifier found it is index 189 in pmdiff2.json. Index 189 is also the one HyperEVM script that differs in the hyperevm unit. Both are full-range swaps cut short by gas, and both chains are on HYPE. Neither unit reran 189 with the largest gas each endpoint grants this cycle.

Contradiction with a lead of theme-reserved-address-routing, which says Monad's 0x08 fails on empty input where the specification returns 1. The critic's eth_call to 0x08 with empty data on https://rpc.monad.xyz (Monad/0.16.7) ran out of gas at 200,000 gas and returned 1 at 327,680 gas, and eth_estimateGas gave 249,120. https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/opcode-pricing lists ecPairing at 225,000 base gas. The behaviour is gas repricing and the result is the specified one. The lead can close.

leads.question: On 8 December 2026 after 15:00 UTC (T14, timestamp 1796742000), which evm2 revision and ruint version does the newest published Tempo release pin in its Cargo.lock? Do battery.py, targeted.py, vec/ruintedges.py and script sets 1, 2 and 6 at the real PoolManager address 0x33620f62c5b9b2086dd6b62f4a297a9f30347029 give the recorded words on the live fork? Repeat on 15 December for T15. This replaces L-905, L-804 and the stablecoin-l1 lead.
leads.why: Tempo has one client, and its integer library rewrote the arithmetic behind FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 48) in October. A wrong word on the live fork would be the network's answer, and no second client would reject the block, so an ordinary swapper could be paid by a wrong price or amount.

leads.question: What do the go1.27 release branch logs on go.googlesource.com list as compiler fixes after go1.27.3, and which of them concern arm64 or amd64 code generation? For each one, does its shape occur in holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 or in core/vm of the Nitro go-ethereum fork, searched with the cycle 18 shapescan tool? Also read whether go1.27.3 has the shapes of Go issues 81863, 81868 and 82839.
leads.why: Arbitrum One answers as a linux-arm64 build made with go1.27.3, and no cycle read the go1.27 fix list. If the sequencer's binary miscompiled an opcode handler used by TickMath, FullMath or SqrtPriceMath, its blocks would be canonical, and an ordinary account could trade against the wrong result.

leads.question: On Robinhood Chain, where the critic saw one three element batch answered by a linux-amd64 build and then a linux-arm64 build, rerun battery.py, targeted.py and pmdiff2.py with each chunk in a batch [web3_clientVersion, eth_call, web3_clientVersion]. Keep a chunk only when both strings name the same architecture, and report the result for amd64 and for arm64 separately. Do the same for Arbitrum One if an amd64 answer ever appears.
leads.why: A miscompile is architecture specific. The Celo pinning method of this cycle shows it can work, and no result on these two chains is known to come from one architecture only.

leads.question: In ruint 1.20.1 (crate from static.crates.io), what do the Shl and Shr implementations for usize and the other primitive types added by #634 compute for amounts 0 to 300, 2^32 and 2^64? Which of them do the SHL, SHR and SAR handlers of revm-interpreter 43.0.2 call? When any public endpoint serves nanoreth nb-20261125-2, or the official endpoint's error texts change, do battery.py and targeted.py still match there?
leads.why: nb-20261125-2 is the first HyperEVM client build on ruint 1.20.1, and operators were asked to run it with hl-node. TickMath.getSqrtPriceAtTick and getTickAtSqrtPrice and the BitMath lookups depend on exact shifts at the edges (src/libraries/TickMath.sol, src/libraries/BitMath.sol).

leads.question: The ruint main CHANGELOG lists under Unreleased the fixes #701 and #704 (a wrong wrapping_from result for negative integers narrower than the Uint) next to #681, the mul_mod fix that shipped as 1.21.1. Which of these fixes do the crate sources of 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 contain? Does revm-interpreter 35 to 43, mega-evm or evm2 call wrapping_from, or any conversion from a signed narrow integer, on an instruction path the PoolManager bytecode reaches (SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD, SAR, i256 helpers, CALLDATALOAD offsets, gas arithmetic that sets the forwarded gas)?
leads.why: The changelog shows a value fault in a released conversion routine that no cycle has traced to an opcode path. A wrong sign conversion in signed division or sign extension would move ticks and tick spacing compression (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:27, src/libraries/TickMath.sol).

leads.question: Re-execute in the public stateless validator every MegaETH block from 32,826,735 to head that holds a PoolManager transaction, with the pre-state tied to the parent root as in cycle 19, and report any block whose post-state root or receipts differ. Rerun battery.py and targeted.py against mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42.
leads.why: The producer is closed and is the only executor whose results become canonical. Mined re-execution is the only public check of it, and it has not run on blocks produced since cycle 19.

leads.question: Which Monad release do validators run on 2026-11-25 (release page, validator announcements), and do battery.py, targeted.py and pmdiff2.py still match on Monad/0.16.7? Also, which emitter or runtime files changed in any Monad tag published after v0.16.7?
leads.why: Validators run compiled native code that simulated calls never reach (rpc/monad_executor.cpp:1296-1300). A change in the emitter after v0.16.7 would reach blocks before any unit read it.

leads.question: On 8 December 2026, after Salvador (Polygon block 98,688,600) and Jenner (BNB Chain 02:30 UTC), which bor and bsc builds do the endpoints report? Do battery.py, targeted.py and both script sets at the real PoolManager addresses give the recorded words, and does any opcode, precompile or keccak cache path changed by the fork release reach the PoolManager bytecode?
leads.why: Both forks change client code on the day, with no unit assigned in cycle 20. A fault there would be canonical for that network.

leads.question: Does any published arc-node artifact (container image labels or digest, a release archive, a checksum file) name the revision behind v0.8.6 and v0.8.6-rc1, so that the value frame hook in crates/evm/src/evm.rs (lines 516-605 on main) can be read at the code that runs? If none does, replay the last 2,000 mined Arc PoolManager transactions that include a native take or a settle with value, using the cycle 13 replay method from parent-block storage, and compare amounts and ERC-6909 balances with the source.
leads.why: Every native payout on Arc passes through custom code whose running revision is not public. A difference there in value accounting or rollback would touch native USDC pools with no attacker-made hook or token.

leads.question: Does pmdiff2 script 189 give the same bytes as Ethereum on Elysium and on HyperEVM when it runs with the largest gas each endpoint grants, or in the split form that cycle 18 used for Tempo?
leads.why: It is the one unexplained difference left on two networks this cycle. Both units attribute it to gas, and neither checked by giving more gas.

leads.question: nanoreth states that receipts of HyperCore system transactions are not covered by the header receipts root. Which earlier HyperEVM clearances (the system transaction census of theme-outside-signature-senders, the sendToEvmWithData ordering, F-044) rest on system transaction data from eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber, and does the commitment that nb-20261125-2 adds agree with what the official endpoint returned for the same blocks?
leads.why: The claim that system transactions run ahead of signed transactions, and never between a user's sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), rests on data the block header does not authenticate.

leads.question: Which earlier Avalanche results seeded PoolManager or token storage with a full state override instead of stateDiff? For each one, does the result still hold when rerun with stateDiff, given that libevm applies state overrides with raw keys and stateDiff overrides with the bit 248 transform?
leads.why: theme-avalanche-multicoin measured that a state override is invisible to extsload and wipes the real storage. A clearance that rested on such a run tested a different storage layout from the one the chain uses.

leads.question: Finish the Upgraded and AdminChanged log scan for the four Elysium bridge proxies created in HyperEVM transaction 0x867cae6d (block 48,956,737) up to head, in windows the endpoint accepts, and name each implementation after the first.
leads.why: If any proxy has moved to an implementation that skips the alias, the F-138 lever would reach ordinary accounts on Elysium. The scan stopped at a batched request limit.

leads.question: Has the MegaETH OptimismPortal2 proxy 0x7f82f57F0Dd546519324392e408b01fcC7D709e8 on Ethereum pointed at any implementation other than 0x55400445e384393f9c1be23e7e734e8d44ed9fd9? Scan its Upgraded events from deployment.
leads.why: If an earlier implementation skipped the alias, deposits sent then could have named the PoolManager as sender. The PoolManager nonce of 1 argues against it but does not exclude a deposit that did not touch the nonce.
